summary.text: Phil Wong represents the 30th District on the New York City Council, which includes Middle Village, Maspeth, Elmhurst, Ridgewood, Glendale and Rego Park in Queens.
His Council biography says he previously served as Budget Director for Council Member Robert Holden and as President of Community Education Council 24.

paragraphs.text: Wong's family immigrated to the United States in 1974, and he has lived in Elmhurst since 1976, according to his Council biography.
He attended public schools in Elmhurst and Maspeth, then graduated from Jamaica High School and Cornell University, and he has three daughters who attended city public schools.
As Community Education Council 24 president he took part in efforts to preserve the Specialized High School Admissions Test, and he was named to City & State's 2021 Education Power 100 list.
The biography says he is a former president of the Chinese American Citizens Alliance and a co-founder of Elmhurst United.
It also says he was a plaintiff in lawsuits including a challenge to New York City's non-citizen voting law and litigation opposing the City of Yes zoning proposal.
